name: INA138NA_3K
title: High-side unipolar current shunt monitor with current output
summary: INA138 and INA168 sense the voltage across a high-side shunt and turn it into an output current of 200 µA per volt. One external resistor to ground converts that current to a voltage and sets a gain anywhere from 1 to beyond 100. Supply and input common-mode voltages are independent, 2.7 V to 36 V for INA138 and 2.7 V to 60 V for INA168, and the parts draw 25 µA typical. Both come in a 5-pin SOT-23 rated -40 °C to 125 °C.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: High-side shunt measurement. The shunt sits between the supply and the load; the two inputs sense the drop across it and the output current, flowing into a single resistor to ground, becomes the output voltage VO = IS × RS × RL / 5 kΩ. The chip's own supply V+ is a separate terminal.

circuits.title: Basic circuit connections
circuits.description: The base connection for both devices. Load current IS from the load supply VP passes through the shunt RS; pin 3 takes the supply end and pin 4 the load end. RL from OUT to ground sets the voltage gain (5 kΩ gives 1, 500 kΩ gives 100) and VO is read across it. V+ may share the load supply or come from its own source, 2.7 V to 36 V (60 V for INA168).

parts.note: load power supply, 2.7 V to 36 V; 60 V with INA168
V+, 2.7 V to 36 V; 60 V with INA168; may be tied to VP

circuits.title: Buffering the output to drive an ADC
circuits.description: The output voltage across RL feeds an OPA340 wired as a unity-gain follower, so the ADC input impedance does not load RL and change the gain. A series resistor and a capacitor to ground after the buffer form a low-pass filter; the capacitor supplies the ADC sampling charge and the resistor keeps the op amp stable. The design target is a 1-MSPS converter. Filter values depend on the op amp and ADC.

circuits.title: Output filter
circuits.description: A capacitor CL across the load resistor RL makes a first-order low-pass filter on the output, with its -3 dB corner at 1 / (2π RL CL). RL is picked for gain first, then CL for the corner. The added capacitance does not make the output unstable.

circuits.title: Offsetting the output voltage with a resistor divider
circuits.description: R1 from a reference VR and R2 to ground both connect to OUT. With no load current the output rests at VR × R2 / (R1 + R2); gain is set by R1 in parallel with R2. Useful on a single supply when the zero-current output should sit at a fraction of the supply.

circuits.title: Offsetting the output voltage with a current source
circuits.description: A REF200 100 µA current source from V+ feeds the OUT node alongside the INA138 output current, so RL carries both. The output offset is 100 µA × RL whatever V+ is, and gain is set by RL alone.

circuits.title: Bipolar current measurement
circuits.description: Two devices sense one 100 mΩ shunt with their inputs crossed, so each one conducts for one direction of the ±1 A load current. Each output passes through a 1N4148 and a 10 kΩ resistor into a shared 100 kΩ resistor to ground, which gives the magnitude at Output with a gain of 20 V/V. The diodes stop the active output from driving into the idle one. A TLV3201 comparator across the two diode cathodes gives the current's sign. Each supply pin has a capacitor to ground.

circuits.title: Bipolar current measurement using the differential input of an ADC
circuits.description: Two INA138s across one shunt with their inputs crossed, each with a 25 kΩ load resistor, feed two inputs of an ADS7870 set for differential conversion. For one current direction one output rises and the other stays at zero, so the sign of the differential reading gives the current's polarity with no extra parts.

circuits.title: Multiplexed measurement using a logic signal for power
circuits.description: Several INA168s, each on its own shunt, share one load resistor RL and one ADS7870 input. Each device's V+ comes from a digital I/O line of the ADS7870, so driving one line high selects that channel. A 1N4148 in series with each output keeps the powered device's current out of the unpowered ones. Two channels are shown; more join the same output bus and I/O lines.
notes: The diode type reads IN4148; the part is a 1N4148.

operation.text: Inside are a high-voltage precision op amp, thin-film resistors trimmed to an absolute value, and a low-noise output transistor. The device runs from one supply, and its inputs may sit above that supply.

The op amp forces the shunt voltage across the 5 kΩ resistor RG1, and the resulting current leaves through Q1's collector at OUT. RL to ground turns it into the output voltage, so the voltage gain is RL / 5 kΩ.

Accurate measurement holds up to 0.5 V across the inputs, which gives 100 µA out; up to 2 V of differential input does no harm. The device is unipolar: pin 3 must be the more positive input. A reversed input gives zero output current and no damage.

The output current stays accurate only within the output's compliance range, set by the supply, the common-mode voltage and the shunt voltage. Its top is the lower of (V+) - 0.7 V - (VIN+ - VIN-) and VIN- - 0.5 V.

A larger RL gives more gain and a narrower bandwidth. Capacitance on OUT narrows it further, so keep that low for the widest response. A capacitor added at the output to filter on purpose does not cause instability.
Running outside the specified supply range, common-mode range or output swing gives unpredictable behaviour. Above 36 V of supply, use INA168.

A larger shunt improves accuracy at low current because offset matters less; a smaller one loses less voltage in the supply line. A full-scale shunt drop of 50 mV to 100 mV suits most designs, and 500 mV is the most that still measures accurately.

RL sets the full-scale output voltage. The output impedance is very high, so RL up to 500 kΩ keeps good accuracy. Anything connected to OUT should have an impedance far above RL, or it changes the gain.

An ADC input appears in parallel with RL and alters the gain, and a dynamic ADC input makes that change hard to predict. An ADC whose input behaves as a resistor to ground can be counted as part of RL. Otherwise a buffer amplifier such as OPA340 between OUT and the ADC removes the loading. Unbuffered, the high output impedance with the ADC's input and sample-and-hold capacitance keeps the sample from settling before the next conversion at 1 MSPS; the buffer allows faster conversion.

The inputs measure correctly above V+: V+ can be 5 V while the load supply is up to 36 V (60 V on INA168), but the output range is limited by the lower of the two. Place a 0.1 µF capacitor near the V+ pin; noisy supplies may need more. No bypass capacitor is needed for stability, but noisy or high-impedance supplies call for decoupling close to the pins.

Run VIN+ and VIN- to the shunt's own pads, as close as possible, so no extra trace resistance adds to the shunt. Measure the output directly across RL, which sits between pin 1 and ground; this matters most in high-current systems where load current flows in the ground. A 0.1 µF capacitor at V+ returns to the ground plane through a via, as do GND and RL.

Two devices across one shunt with their inputs reversed measure current in both directions: only one conducts at a time. In the comparator version a 100 kΩ output resistor gives 20 V/V, 10 kΩ resistors in series with each output develop the comparator's input voltage, and diodes keep the active output's current out of the idle one.
INA138-Q1 and INA168-Q1 are the AEC-Q100 qualified versions.
